**Navigating the Digital Age: Social Media’s Impact on the Young Mind** (URL: [https://www.brooklane.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Susan-Corley-Navigating-The-Digital-Age-Social-Media-Impact-on-Young-Minds.pdf](https://www.brooklane.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Susan-Corley-Navigating-The-Digital-Age-Social-Media-Impact-on-Young-Minds.pdf))   
*Published March 2025* 

*(Note: Source is a 44-slide PPT, not a news/research article)*

* *Why Talk about Social Media and its Impact on Youth?*  
  * Children/adolescents/young adults are among the largest users of social media  
  * Social media is a medium of communication, learning, and entertainment for children & adolescents  
  * Adolescents spend 5+ hours per day on social media  
    * Often logging into their favorite social media sites 100+ times per day  
  * Most sites not designed with their safety in mind  
  * Preteens/teens at an age where they have difficulty regulating & expressing emotions  
    * Hugely susceptible to peer pressure  
  * Risks associated with online/media use  
    * E.g., social media provides opportunities for online expressings of offline behaviors like bullying, clique forming, and sexual experimentation  
      * Potentially exposing them to problems like cyberbullying, sexting, privacy issues, and potential addiction and sleep deprivation. Young brain struggles to understand violence and pornography  
* *Why is Social Media So Appealing?*  
  * Ability to share information quickly  
  * Adolescents experience independence, social consciousness, identity, & connection  
  * Provides instant gratification that teens seek  
    * Particularly when receiving notifications by others via posts, likes, hearts, thumbs up, etc.  
      * These are signals that provide short-term reward – the increase in dopamine impacts perception of importance, value, & truth to what they are seeing  
* *Popular Social Media Sites for Youth:*  
  * TikTok  
  * Snapchat  
  * Instagram  
  * YouTube  
  * Reddit  
  * Discord  
* *“4 Critical Factors: Healthy Child Development”*  
  * Movement   
  * Touch  
  * Human Connection  
  * Exposure to Nature  
* *“4 Essentials For Teen Brain Development”*  
  * Blossoming  
  * Pruning   
  * Myelination   
  * Hormones  
* *Benefits of Social Media*  
  * Builds technical skills/competent citizens in a digital age  
  * Hastens and increases communication  
  * Enhances social connections  
    * Extends friendships/network/study groups  
    * Can be supportive  
    * Connects peers with teams, clubs, etc.  
  * Virtual empathy and compassion  
  * Platform for shared interests, social networking  
  * Enhanced learning opportunities & creativity  
    * Share music, art, etc.  
    * Key source of information/connection with educators  
    * Peer-based learning  
    * Broader perspectives of other cultures around the globe  
    * Volunteering/community involvement outreach  
  * Key source of information to assess important and/or technical things (e.g., health information)  
* *Flipsides of Social Media Use*  
  * Cyberbullying  
  * Privacy/safety  
  * Risk reputation  
  * Mental health and well-being  
  * Inappropriate/harmful content  
  * Time drain  
* *Social Media and Mental Health*  
  * Parental involvement and intervention can have a positive impact on mental health  
    * Strong parent/child/teen connections can help absorb harm from content exposure  
  * Children and teens with low life satisfaction more at risk  
  * Video/scrolling centered platforms may pose bigger risk to children and teens because of the never-ending loop of content  
  * Texting provides immediate gratification and can be a significant anxiety producer  
    ![][image1]  
* *Cyberbullying and mental health*  
  * Correlation between cyberbullying, anxiety and depression  
  * Apps like Snapchat, Reddit, and Instagram have the highest frequency of target cyberbullying  
    * NOTE: unverified claim w/o source  
  * Females more often than males are the targets of cyberbullying  
    * NOTE: unverified claim w/o source  
  * Victims report loss of self-esteem and withdraw  
    * They also report school avoidance, high absenteeism, deteriorating grades and behavioral problems  
    * NOTE: unverified claim w/o source  
  * Depression levels increased in most cases, for those with pre-existing depression  
    * NOTE: unverified claim w/o source  
  * Increasing numbers of individuals reporting self-harm and suicidal ideation as the result of cyberbullying  
    * NOTE: unverified claim w/o source  
  * Youth are encouraged to engage in risky behaviors online that can also result in death or serious injury as a part of the pressure from online individuals  
* *Sexting*  
  * Definition: the sharing of sexually explicit images, videos, or messages through electronic means  
  * Study showed that sexting has become more common among adolescents  
    * Results indicate at least 1 in 4 teens are receiving sexually explicit texts and emails, at least 1 in 7 are sending sexts, more than 1 in 10 teens are forwarding sexts without consent, and about 1 in 12 teens have had sexts they’ve sent forwarded without their consent  
* *Impact of Excessive Amounts on Children*  
  * Increase in technology leads to sedentary lifestyle, weight and health issues early  
    * NOTE: unverified claim w/o source  
  * Impacts concentration, focus for learning  
  * Not enough reading, creative play, and games can impact their preparedness to cope with changes in tech and society over time  
    * NOTE: unverified claim w/o source  
  * Increase in dysregulated behaviors  
    * NOTE: unverified claim w/o source  
* *Problematic Interactive Media Use: PIMU*  
  * PIMU \= term coined by Michael Rich, MD “the Mediatrician” and colleagues  
  * Overuse of a necessary resource  
  * Driven by psychological disorders–ADHD, anxiety, etc.  
  * Continued use despite negative consequences  
  * Goal of treatment: self-regulation  
    * Similar to treating Binge Eating Disorder  
  * Inability to regulate use of interactive media with negative effects on key elements of their lives including:  
    * Sleep  
    * Nutrition   
    * Academic performance  
    * Social life  
    * Relationships  
    * Mental health  
* *Presentation of PIMU*  
  * Video gaming  
    * Excessive gaming on computer, console, or multiple devices  
    * Disrupts sleep, homework, meals, family time, face-to-face interactions and exercise  
    * Appearance of defiant and aggressive behavior when asked to stop  
  * Social Media  
    * Use of social media as main means of connecting with others  
    * Limited face to face communication with others  
    * Doom scrolling  
    * Cyberbullying  
    * Sexting  
  * Info Bingeing  
    * Following threads of online forums and blogs  
    * Binge watching short and long-term videos  
    * Doing so in place of other activities   
  * Pornography  
    * Used to meet sexual needs  
    * Creates slowing and confusion in sexual development  
* *COVID Impact*  
  * Increased use of social media and the consequences of that for all age groups  
  * Online schooling  
  * More gaming (moving social interactions to virtual space)  
  * Accelerated mental health issues  
* *Today’s World*  
  * Growing up in today’s society means regularly engaging with technology  
  * During the pandemic, screen time increased, both out of necessity during remote schooling and for connection  
    * Use has remained high  
  * Technology and media are important tools for social connection, education, entertainment, and advocacy that pervade the daily lives of children and teens  
    * Necessary for them to understand how to use these tools and be good citizens in the digital world  
* *Digital Citizenship*  
  * Helps kids and teens be safe and secure online and in digital spaces  
  * Dangers of sharing personal information online  
  * Importance of password protection  
  * Reduction of identity fraud  
  * How to protect self from less defined digital threats, like reputation  
  * Privacy and reputation   
  * Knowledge around digital footprint   
* *Self Discovery Directs Change*  
  * Education  
  * How use matters/evaluation  
    * Screening questions  
    * Understanding how long-term use impacts mental health and life  
* *Self Discovery \- Questions for Teens to Ask Themselves/Consider*  
  * What do particular social media (apps, platforms) mean to you, do for you? (escapism, boredom, relief, find identity, connect with peers, etc.)  
  * What are some challenges you have encountered?  
  * What do you like about social media?  
  * What makes a good video?  
  * What type of videos do you engage with most? (algorithms)  
* *Education/Self-Discovery*  
  * How use matters:  
    * Why do you use social media?  
    * How does it make you feel?  
    * What are your favorite social media sites?  
    * What do you like best?  
    * What isn’t so great about it?  
    * When not connected with tech, who do you hang out with?  
    * Are you craving the connection?  
    * Do you constantly catch yourself checking it or feeling internal pressure to check social media?  
    * Does it create anxiety when you are on the media?  
    * Do you feel FOMO (fear of missing out) or FOBLO (fear of being left out)?  
* *Teen Self-Reflection*  
  * Help teens recognize the limitations of social media and that too much social media time distracts from engaging in more meaningful interactions  
  * Encourage teens to increase more face-to-face communication times with friends and others  
    * Direct vs. indirect communication  
  * Ask teens to evaluate underlying reasons/needs to use social media, what triggers their use, needs, beliefs about social media, and their use   
    * What do they think is overuse?  
    * Are they experiencing negative effects as a result of their social media use?  
* *A Matter of Balance*  
  * One’s social media well-being is based on how they use it  
  * Are social networks being used to connect or compare?  
  * Humans are social beings; our brains are wired to connect and social media encourages sharing and connecting  
    * Especially important for teens  
  * Disconnect from reality – “escapism”  
* *Teach to Upgrade One by One*  
  * Text to call \-\> call to video \-\> video to in-person (face-to-face)   
    * This applies to people who are NOT strangers you met on the internet   
* *Social-Emotional Skills (3 skills essential for both offline and online interactions)*  
  * Empathy  
  * Kindness  
  * Personal responsibility  
* *Rules of Regulation*  
  * Shift of perception  
  * Technology, phone, and social media free times (an app breakfree-tracks time on your phone)  
  * Delete some social media  
  * Engage in other activities that increase social skills, healthy interests, and hobbies (non-technology related)  
  * Develop skills that are lacking and driving indulgent use of social media  
  * Develop boredom  
* *Empathy Building Skills*  
  * “It’s not about you, it’s about the people around you”  
  * Try and put yourself in the other person’s shoes  
  * Practice empathy in everyday life  
  * Essence of relationship building:  
    * Empathy  
    * Respect  
    * Warmth   
    * Genuineness  
* *Best Practices for Adolescent Social Media Use*  
  * Think before you post  
  * Follow the WWGS (What Would Grandma Say) rule  
  * Assume what is posted isn’t private, even if it is sent as a private message  
  * Realize what is posted is *permanent*, even if it is deleted (educate yourself about digital footprints)  
  * Be aware of how online activity affects their future and reputation (professional and personal)  
  * Life over “likes”  
  * Moderation   
* *Guide for Parents*  
  * Caution: restricting or stalking may be counterproductive  
  * Encourage parents to:  
    * Become more social media educated  
    * Be a healthy role model of media uses at home  
    * Encourage times to do other healthy activities: exercise, outside the home activities  
    * Have regular conversations with their teen(s) about online use and discuss issues specific to the challenges faced by today’s adolescents on social media  
    * Use media with teens: learn and teach  
    * Devices are tools, not treats  
* *Digital Wellness*  
  * “Digital Wellness is an intentional state of physical, mental, and social health that occurs within mindful engagement in the digital and natural environment.” –Michael Rich, MD   
* *5 M’s of Digital Wellness*  
  * Model–Be the change you want to see  
  * Mentor–Responsible, respectful, digital contract  
  * Monitor–Do not be the digital police  
  * Memories–Make them IRL  
  * Mastery–Guardrails, mindfully  
* *Instead of Developing Killer Apps, Develop Killer BEs*  
  * Be balanced  
  * Be mindful  
  * Be present
